task: List Steven Bonta's proposed deciphered signs
approach: Reused the existing 2024 manuscript text and checked every category against the five visual sign-table slides in Lecture 7.
challenges: The retained manuscript text omits glyphs, so labels alone do not identify visual forms.
Automatic captions misrender several Sanskrit words.
YouTube advertisements delayed access; a browser click timed out.
fixes: Inspected the lecture slides at 25:39, 27:24, 29:04, 29:54 and 30:29.
Read the printed labels and sound alternatives directly from the slides and compared them with Table 18.
Used the player keyboard controls after inspecting the failed click state.
outcome: 58 labelled entries occur in each version. The union has 59: BALAPATI/PALAPATI is in Lecture 7, while KARAPALA is in the manuscript table. Entries can group several visual variants, so these counts do not resolve his separate claim of about 55–56 deciphered signs.
limits: Visual descriptions are identification aids, not catalogue crosswalks. KARAPALA's glyph remains unverified. Fish and oval measurement families without assigned readings are outside this phonetic/logographic table. No corpus replication or validation of the proposed sounds was performed.
identity_discrepancy: Lecture 7 at 27:24 labels the bow alone DAna1 and the person with a bow DAna2. The earlier provisional claim ledger Q072 associates DAna1 with the person-with-bow role. Full manuscript figures are needed to determine whether this is a version change or a ledger association error; the earlier computational endpoint has not been edited.
